q-71371.name: Question 1
q-71371.worked_solution:
First, we re-write the expression as a square:

$$
\sqrt{12}\cdot \sqrt{12}={(\sqrt{12})}^{2}.
$$

Now, recall that the square and the square root cancel each other out. So, we have

$$
{(\sqrt{12})}^{2}=12.
$$

q-99282.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the expression as a square:

$$

$$

$$

?

Find 23⋅8⋅23⋅8⋅23.

a
4
b
8
c
16
d
2 048
e
12
Submit
Correct

We have 23⋅8⋅23⋅8⋅23=(23⋅23⋅23)(8⋅8)=(23)3(8)2=2⋅8=16.

q-71375.name: Question 5
q-71375.worked_solution:

$$
\sqrt[3]{-6}\cdot \sqrt[3]{-6}\cdot \sqrt[3]{-6}={(\sqrt[3]{-6})}^{3}.
$$

Now, we use that  the cube and the cube root cancel each other out. So, we have

$$
{(\sqrt[3]{-6})}^{3}=-6.
$$
